defects_found: The chrome overflowed the page at 320 px with a long workspace name: .collab-switcher and .collab-account are flex items and default to min-width auto, so the context name could not shrink and its ellipsis never applied. CF-P7-012 could not see it because it qualified the switcher on its own, with no flex parent to refuse; the composed chrome is the only place it appears.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.journey: invite someone and have them accept
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: a second real GitHub account to invite
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: The controls are wired and the routes answer, but qualifying acceptance end to end needs a second person signing in to their own account and binding their own device. The invitation.created and invitation.accepted rows in the Preview database are from the CF-P6-008 and G2-G3 qualification runs of earlier phases and are not claimed by this story.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: two devices editing one workspace document at the same time
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: The dialog and its resolution vocabulary are built and gated, but reaching one needs concurrent edits to a document, and the document surfaces are not among the twelve CF-P7-001 froze for this phase. It stays absent-by-state, which is what the surface renders.

declared_limits.sync_reason: Saving, Offline, and Conflict are all derived from outbox entries for an open document, and there is no document surface in the frozen inventory to create one. Saved and Access removed do not need one: Saved is the empty queue, and Access removed is reached from a real workspace-scoped denial followed by a membership re-check, which this build performs.

previously_declared_now_closed.note: Five limits recorded on 2026-07-26 said these journeys could not complete in the build as it then stood. Four were closed by building what was missing and one by the owner doing what no agent may: all are now qualified and recorded under qualified_journeys.completed.

limits.was_missing: an unlock secret to protect the device key
limits.closed_by: js/collaboration/device-record.js generates one per browser and stores it with the device record. An accepted MVP tradeoff over a passphrase surface, taken with the owner on the record; devices table shows 9 registrations.

limits.was_missing: a client-side workspace-DEK sealer, and an active device to seal to
limits.closed_by: js/collaboration/workspace-key-envelope.js ports wrapWorkspaceKey to the browser and is verified against the server's own unwrapWorkspaceKey; 7 workspaces and 10 unrevoked envelopes exist in Preview D1.

limits.was_missing: an active device to bind the membership to
limits.closed_by: Partially: an active device now exists, so this is no longer what blocks it. It remains not completable for a different and honest reason -- there is no second account -- and is re-declared above under that reason rather than dropped.

limits.was_missing: an actual signed-in GitHub session, which no agent may obtain
limits.closed_by: The owner signed in themselves. This limit was always going to be closed by a person rather than by code, and it was.

qualified_journeys.driven_by: the Product Owner, in their own browser, signed in to their own GitHub account
qualified_journeys.why_not_an_agent: Qualifying these journeys needs a real OAuth session, and obtaining one means entering credentials at github.com. No agent did so at any point; every step below was performed by the owner and is corroborated here by read-only queries against the Preview D1 database rather than by anything an agent could have written.
qualified_journeys.spanned_builds: The journey was driven across successive Preview builds while defects it exposed were fixed. Workspace creation first completed on 06c53f9f (218927c); the member list first rendered on 1c2cea77 (0b9455b); the state recorded here was re-confirmed by the owner on the deployment named above. The workspaces persist in D1, so every build after creation observes the same records.

completed.evidence: A session cookie was issued and GET /api/v1/session answered authenticated: true with the owner login. The composed chrome rendered the account trigger with that login.

devices table: 9 rows, 1 active and 8 revoked. Each registration generated a P-256 key pair in the browser, protected it under a locally generated unlock secret, sent only the public JWK, and re-bound the local key onto the device id the server assigned. The surface rendered the fingerprint in four-character groups.

workspaces table: 7 workspaces created through this UI (ádsadasd, đâsdasd, sádasdasd, ádasdas x2, ádasdasdas, ádasdasdasd), each at current_key_version 1 with the creator as its single member. audit_events records workspace.created x10 across the database. workspace_key_envelopes holds 10 unrevoked envelopes, which is the part that could not be faked: each was sealed in the browser by js/collaboration/workspace-key-envelope.js and accepted by the server parser, so the ECDH/HKDF/AES-GCM port agrees with functions/_lib/e2ee byte for byte on live data.
devices table: 8 rows in state revoked. The server was called first and the local key deleted only after it accepted, so a failed revocation leaves the device working rather than half dead.

Owner-reported: after switching, both the context indicator and the panel below it showed the newly selected workspace. This is U2 exercised against live data rather than a fixture — the half of U2 that is easiest to lose is the panel following the chrome, and it did.

not_completed.journey: invite someone and have them accept
not_completed.reason: Not attempted. It needs a second real GitHub account, and the invitation.created/invitation.accepted rows present in this database are from the CF-P6-008 and G2-G3 qualification runs of earlier phases, not from this one. Nothing here claims otherwise.
Not reachable: it needs two devices editing one document concurrently, and the document surfaces are not part of Phase 7.

qualified_journeys.defects_this_journey_exposed: Seven, each found only by a real signed-in session and each fixed and pushed during it: resolveSession read an enveloped body for a route that answers unenveloped (so authenticated was always false); beginSignIn had the same defect; every mutation with no body omitted Content-Type and was refused 415; the acting-device header was never sent; create-workspace and device-initialization disagreed on device.state vs device.status; the create-workspace submit control could never enable because its model was only told the typed name on submit; and the member list refused every row because it read a keyReadiness field the route does not send. None was visible to any test in the repository beforehand.
